rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says ḥuqb means an age or eternity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الحقب الدهر. وقال عبد الله بن عمرو

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr and Abu Hurayra say a ḥuqb is eighty years.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو وأبو هريرة: ثمانون سنة.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a ḥuqb is seventy years.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: سبعون. وقيل: سنة بلغة قريش

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reports that Quraysh used ḥuqb for one year.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سنة بلغة قريش ذكره الفراء. وقيل: وقت غير محدود

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says it can mean an unspecified period.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وقت غير محدود قاله أبو عبيدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates reaching the meeting of the seas with traveling for a long age: Moses will persist until either occurs.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله أو أمضي معطوف على أبلغ فغيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing makes the age a limit on “I will not cease”: Moses will continue until he is sure he has missed the meeting place.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي تغيية لقوله لا أبرح كقولك لا أفارقك

rows.speaker: الضحاك والجمهور
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reads ḥuquban with a still qāf, while the majority read it with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك حقبا بإسكان القاف والجمهور بضمها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted clause says Moses and his attendant traveled before reaching the meeting of the two seas.
rows.anchor: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما ثم جملة محذوفة التقدير فسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Moses of a servant at the meeting place more learned than he; Moses was to carry a fish in a basket as a sign of where to find him.
rows.anchor: إن لي عبدا بمجمع البحرين هو أعلم منك. قال موسى: يا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Joshua carried the fish; at the rock they slept, and it escaped into the sea while God held back the water so its path formed an arch.
rows.anchor: فنام موسى واضطرب الحوت في المكتل فخرج منه فسقط في البحر سربا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports variously say the fish was salted, grilled, or fresh.
rows.anchor: قيل: وكان الحوت مالحا. وقيل: مشويا. وقيل: طريا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Joshua collected fish and bread, and the fish revived by the spring of life while Moses slept; another says the travelers ate from it, while water from Joshua’s ablution revived it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جمع يوشع الحوت والخبز في مكتل فنزلا ليلة على شاطئ عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording attributes forgetting to both Moses and his attendant; another view assigns the lapse to Joshua, who saw the fish escape but delayed telling Moses and then forgot.
rows.anchor: والظاهر نسبة النسيان إلى موسى وفتاه. وقيل: كان النسيان من أحدهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Joshua forgot to offer the fish and Moses forgot to instruct him about it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نسي يوشع أن يقدمه، ونسي موسى أن يأمر فيه بشيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted noun: one of the two forgot.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو على حذف مضاف أي نسي أحدهما. وقال الزمخشري:

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says they forgot to inspect the fish and what might happen to it, which had been made a sign of finding what they sought.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أي نسيا تفقد أمره وما يكون منه مما جعل أمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish’s path resembled a tunnel because the water did not close behind it but remained like an arch, as in the hadith.
rows.anchor: وشبه بالسرب مسلك الحوت في الماء حين لم ينطبق الماء بعده بل بقي كالطاق،

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the fish’s path remained empty.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: بقي موضع سلوكه فارغا. وقال قتادة: ماء جامدا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the water became solid.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ماء جامدا وعن ابن عباس: حجرا صلدا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the water became hard stone.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: حجرا صلدا. وقال ابن زيد: إنما اتخذ سبيله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fish went over land to the sea and then swam normally; he reads saraban as free roaming, like a grazing camel or the verse’s “moving by day.”
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إنما اتخذ سبيله سربا في البر حتى وصل إلى البحر

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the fish tunneled through the earth from the basket and pierced a stone in its way.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: اتخذ سربا في التراب من المكتمل، وصادف في طريقه حجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading places the passage in water; a sound hadith says the water formed an arch, a miracle if Moses or Khidr was a prophet and otherwise a marvel of sanctity.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن السرب كان في الماء ولا يفسر إلا بما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound hadith describes the water forming an arch above the fish’s route.
rows.anchor: ورد في الحديث الصحيح أن الماء صار عليه كالطاق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says the track became a stone road that Moses followed to an island where he found Khidr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عاد موضع سلوك الحوت حجرا طريقا وأن موسى مشى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When they passed” refers to the meeting of the seas; al-Zamakhshari instead says it means the rock, their appointment place.
rows.anchor: فلما جاوزا أي مجمع البحرين. وقال الزمخشري: الموعد وهو الصخرة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They traveled from the rock through the night and until midday, when Moses became hungry and tired, remembered the fish, and asked for it; this journey means the stretch beyond the rock.
rows.anchor: قيل: سارا بعد مجاوزة الصخرة الليلة والغد إلى الظهر

rows.speaker: الجمهور وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: The majority read naṣaban with two fatḥas; Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr uses two ḍammas, one of four dialect forms cited by al-Lawāmiʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نصبا بفتحتين وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير بضمتين.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why Joshua forgot a clear sign through a night’s journey; he answers that Satan distracted him and repeated marvels had become familiar, reducing his concern.
rows.anchor: قلت: قد شغله الشيطان بوساوسه فذهب بفكره كل

rows.speaker: أبو بكر غالب بن عطية
rows.claim: Abu Bakr Ghalib ibn Atiyya quotes Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari: Moses needed no food during forty days of communion, but felt hunger within part of a day while walking to meet a human.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر غالب بن عطية والداني عبد الحق المفسر: سمعت أبا الفضل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes araʾayta as “tell me”: Joshua recalls what he saw at the rock and his lapse, then asks Moses what befell him; the wording omits part of his question.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أرأيت بمعنى أخبرني فإن قلت: فما وجه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh is cited for araʾaytaka meaning “inform me.”
rows.anchor: وكون أرأيتك بمعنى أخبرني ذكره سيبويه: وقد أمعنا الكلام

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says Arabs used araʾaytaka for “inform me,” sometimes dropping its hamza, unlike the sense “did you see?”.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الحسن الأخفش: إن العرب أخرجتها عن معناها

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the “inform me” construction takes an object of inquiry and an interrogative clause, and its address suffix is fixed.
rows.anchor: وإذا كانت بمعنى أخبرني فلا بد بعدها من الاسم المستخبر عنه

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash takes the fāʾ as proof that araʾayta here shifted toward “as for” or an attention-getting use: “As for when we sheltered at the rock, I forgot the fish.”
rows.anchor: بدليل دخول الفاء ألا ترى قوله أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says fāʾ answers araʾayta because idh cannot be conditional unless accompanied by mā.
rows.anchor: وليست الفاء إلا جوابا لأرأيت، لأن إذ لا يصح أن يجازى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that al-Zamakhshari’s “inform me” parse lacks the required object of inquiry and following interrogative.
rows.anchor: وفيه إن أرأيت إذا كانت بمعنى أخبرني فلا بد بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I forgot the fish” means Joshua forgot to mention what had happened to it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نسيت الحوت نسيت ذكر ما جرى فيه لك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joshua’s attributing his forgetting to Satan’s whispering shows good adab in assigning the cause of a lapse.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان حسن أدب سبب النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase an adhkurahu is a بدل اشتمال attached to the pronoun referring to the fish.
rows.anchor: وأن أذكره بدل اشتمال من الضمير العائد على الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent pronoun in “it took its way” refers to the fish as in the earlier wording, and the statement is Joshua’s.
rows.anchor: في واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا عائد على الحوت كما عاد في

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير عائد على موسى أي اتخذ موسى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjaban means either that one marvels at it or that its route was astonishing because its trace remained as far as it traveled.
rows.anchor: ومعنى عجبا أي تعجب من ذلك أو اتخاذا عجبا وهو أن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the path as marvellous because it resembled a tunnel, or takes ʿajaban as Joshua’s closing exclamation at the wonder he saw and forgot.
rows.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري سبيله عجبا وهو كونه شبيه السرب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes ʿajaban Moses’ exclamation, but Abu Hayyan does not accept it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن عجبا حكاية لتعجب موسى وليس بذلك انتهى.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Joshua may report that the fish made an astonishing route for people, or finish the report and then personally exclaim at its revival after part was eaten.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا يحتمل أن يكون

rows.speaker: أبو شجاع
rows.claim: Abu Shujaʿ, in a book of al-Tabari, says he saw it as half a fish with one eye and no other half.
rows.anchor: قال أبو شجاع في كتاب الطبري رأيته أتيت به فإذا هو شق حوت

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says he personally saw a fish half with a thin covering over the flesh and no bone beneath it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأنا رأيته والشق الذي فيه شي عليه قشرة رقيقة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya also allows divine narration: either Moses marveled at following the fish or the fish’s route was wondrous to people.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون واتخذ سبيله الآية إخبارا من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: حفص والكسائي
rows.claim: Hafs reads the hāʾ in ansānihi with ḍamma in connected recitation; al-Kisaʾi inclines the sīn’s fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص: وما أنسانيه بضم الهاء وفي الفتح عليه الله وذلك

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah’s codex and reading have “except Satan made me forget to mention it.”
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله وقراءته أن أذكره إلا الشيطان.

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads ittikhādh sabīlihi as a verbal noun coordinated with the object pronoun in an adhkurahu.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: واتخاذ سبيله عطف على المصدر على ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the fish’s loss and its path through the sea, the sign of finding the righteous servant; the object of “seek” is omitted.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بقوله ذلك إلى أمر الحوت وفقده واتخاذه سبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr, al-Kisaʾi, and Nafiʿ retain the yāʾ of nabghi in connected reading; the author says retention is better.
rows.anchor: وقرئ نبغ بغير ياء في الوصل وإثباتها أحسن وهي قراءة أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yāʾ both in connection and at pause; most omit it at pause to follow the codex spelling.
rows.anchor: وأما الوقف فالأكثر فيه طرح الياء اتباعا لرسم المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They retraced their steps tracking their footprints; qaṣaṣan is either an implied verbal noun or a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: فارتدا رجعا على أدراجهما من حيث جاءا. قصصا أي يقصان الأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him a servant from God’s servants is an honorific addition expressing special distinction.
rows.anchor: عبدا من عبادنا هذه إضافة تشريف واختصاص،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found the servant at the rock where the fish was lost, lying under his garment; Moses greets him and they discuss their different divinely given knowledge.
rows.anchor: وجداه عند الصخرة التي فقد الحوت عندها وهو مسجى في ثوبه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify him as al-Khidr; other reports name al-Yasaʿ, Ilyas, Khidrun son of Qabil, or Bilya ibn Malkan.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنه الخضر وخالف من لا يعتد بخلافه فزعم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say Khidr was a prophet taught revealed inner realities, while Moses knew legal rulings and outward judgments.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن الخضر نبي وكان علمه معرفة بواطن قد أوحيت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says Khidr was named after sitting on a worn hide that turned green beneath him.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث سمي خضرا لأنه جلس على فروة بالية فاهتزت تحته خضراء.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other reports explain his name by the ground turning green when he prayed or by him sitting on elevated white or hard ground that turned green.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان إذا صلى اخضر ما حوله. وقيل: جلس على فروة بيضاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports say his mother was Roman and his father Persian, or make him a king’s son who refused succession and fled to sea islands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت أمه رومية وأبوه فارسي. وقيل: كان ابن ملك من الملوك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say Khidr died.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنه مات. وقال شرف الدين أبو عبد الله

rows.speaker: شرف الدين أبو عبد الله محمد بن أبي الفضل المرسي
rows.claim: Al-Mursi argues Khidr is not alive; otherwise he would have had to come to Muhammad, believe in him, and follow him, citing a report about Moses and Jesus following Muhammad if alive.
rows.anchor: وقال شرف الدين أبو عبد الله محمد بن أبي الفضل المرسي: أما خضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan notes the cited hadith may refer only to Moses, while Muslims hold Jesus is alive and will descend.
rows.anchor: انتهى هكذا أوراد لحديث ومذهب المسلمين أن عيسى حي وأنه ينزل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The mercy God gave Khidr is interpreted as revelation and prophethood, or as provision.
rows.anchor: والرحمة التي آتاه الله إياها هي الوحي والنبوة. وقيل: الرزق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge from God means knowledge reserved to Him, specifically information about the unseen.
rows.anchor: وعلمناه من لدنا علما أي من عندنا أي مما يختص بنا من العلم

rows.speaker: أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Zayd transmits from Abu Amr a light-nūn reading of min ladunā, a dialect form of ladun, said to be its original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو من لدنا بتخفيف النون وهي لغة في لدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan criticizes people claiming private inspired knowledge that certifies companions for Paradise or identifies someone as Khidr.
rows.anchor: قيل: وقد أولع كثير ممن ينتمي إلى الصلاح بادعاء هذا العلم

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح ابن دقيق العيد
rows.claim: Ibn Daqiq al-Idd recounted a teacher’s claim to have seen Khidr; when asked how he knew the man was Khidr, the teacher fell silent.
rows.anchor: وكان قاضي القضاة أبو الفتح محمد بن علي بن مطيع القشيري المعروف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Khidriyya is a rank saints inherit in Khidr’s footsteps; Abdul Wahid al-Abbasi’s Hanbali companions believed he met Khidr.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم يزعم أن الخضرية رتبة يتولاها بعض الصالحين على قدم الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits the meeting and exchange of words before Moses asks to follow Khidr, as in the authentic hadith.
rows.anchor: قال له موسى في الكلام محذوف تقديره فلما التقيا وتراجعا الكلام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr told Ibn Abbas that Nauf claimed Khidr was not Moses’ companion and Moses was Ibn Misha; Ibn Abbas called Nauf an enemy of God and a liar.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير إنه قال لابن عباس: إن نوفا ابن امرأة كعب

rows.speaker: الحسن والزهري وأبو بحرية وابن محيصن وابن مناذر ويعقوب وأبو عبيد واليزيدي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce rushdan with two fatḥas; this is also Abu Amr’s reading among the seven.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري وأبو بحرية وابن محيصن وابن مناذر ويعقوب

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The remaining canonical readers use ḍamma on rāʾ and sukūn on shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة بضم الراء وإسكان الشين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr emphatically predicts Moses cannot endure because the actions look objectionable even to a righteous person; patience is especially unlikely without knowledge, which excuses Moses under his own law.
rows.anchor: ونفى الخضر استطاعة الصبر معه على سبيل التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khubran is either accusative of specification or a verbal noun used because the phrase means “what you have not been informed of”; Hasan and Ibn Hurmuz read the bāʾ with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وانتصب خبرا على التمييز أي مما لم يحط به خبرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses conditions his promise of patience on God’s will because he expects difficulty; wa-lā aʿṣī may coordinate with ṣābiran or with ستجدني, outside the expressed condition.
rows.anchor: قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا وعده بوجدانه صابرا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says Moses fulfilled his conditional promise of patience but broke his unconditional promise not to disobey by asking questions; Abu Hayyan says this depends on linking wa-lā aʿṣī to ستجدني.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري: وعد موسى من نفسه بشيئين: بالصبر وقرنه بالاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr tells Moses to withhold questions about an unclear action until Khidr begins explaining; this models a student’s etiquette with a teacher.
rows.anchor: فلا تفاتحني بالسؤال حتى أكون أنا الفاتح عليك، وهذا من أدب

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Ibn Amir read without hamza; Abu Jaʿfar opens sīn and lām and doubles nūn, while the rest of the seven use hamza and a light nūn; a rare report from Ibn Amir drops yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر فلا تسئلني وعن أبي جعفر بفتح السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recaps the boat, boy, and wall incidents and the related dialogue before Khidr explains them.
rows.anchor: فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة خرقها قال أخرقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Khidr traveled with Joshua, unmentioned because he was a follower; another view says Moses sent him back to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: فانطلقا أي موسى والخضر وكان معهم يوشع ولم يضمر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Moses dismissed Joshua and returned him to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان موسى قد صرفه ورده إلى بني إسرائيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in السفينة is generic because no particular ship was previously specified.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في السفينة لتعريف الجنس إذ لم يتقدم عهد

rows.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
rows.claim: Their sound hadith says the two walked along the shore, asked a passing vessel for passage, and were carried free because its crew recognized Khidr; Khidr then removed a plank with an adze.
rows.anchor: رواه البخاري ومسلم في صحيحهما قالا: «فانطلقا يمشيان على ساحل البحر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Moses’ first objection came from forgetfulness; Khidr also compares their knowledge to the tiny amount a sparrow removed from the sea.
rows.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وكان الأول من موسى نسيانا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The lām in li-tughriqa is read as either a consequence lām or a lām of purpose.
rows.anchor: واللام في لتغرق أهلها. قيل: لام العاقبة. وقيل: لام العلة.

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو عبيد
rows.claim: These readers use an active third-person verb with nominative ahluhā; the other seven use a second-person verb with accusative ahlahā, and Hasan and Abu Rajaʾ double the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading takes Moses’ “what I forgot” literally: he forgot the agreement not to ask before Khidr explained.
rows.anchor: والظاهر حمل النسيان على وضعه. وقد قال عليه السلام: «كانت الأولى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say Moses forgot the agreement between them.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الجمهور. وعن أبي ابن كعب أنه ما نسي

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says Moses did not forget but used indirect speech.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ابن كعب أنه ما نسي ولكن قوله هذا من معاريض الكلام.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers literal forgetfulness, an indirect face-saving claim, or nisyān meaning leaving the earlier instruction; he compares the indirect form with Abraham’s words.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أراد أنه نسي وصيته ولا مؤاخذة على الناسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan relies only on the Prophet’s report that Moses’ first objection was forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: ولا يعتمد إلا قول الرسول: «كانت الأولى من موسى نسيانا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La turhiqnī means do not overwhelm or burden me with difficulty in following you; Moses asks Khidr to make the journey easy and leave off disputation.
rows.anchor: ولا ترهقني لا تغشني وتكلفني من أمري وهو اتباعك عسرا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads ʿusran with ḍamma on the sīn wherever it occurs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر عسرا بضم السين حيث وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted clause says they left the ship without drowning anyone; on shore Khidr saw a boy playing and killed him, with reports differing on the method.
rows.anchor: فانطلقا في الكلام حذف تقديره فخرجا من السفينة ولم يقع غرق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports variously say Khidr crushed the boy with a stone, slaughtered him, snapped his neck, or struck his head against a wall.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رضه بحجر. وقيل: ذبحه. وقيل: فتل عنقه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the boy had not reached puberty, explaining Moses’ description of him as pure; others say he was an adult because Arabic continues using ghulām for a young man.
rows.anchor: قيل: وكان هذا الغلام لم يبلغ الحلم ولهذا قال: أقتلت نفسا

rows.speaker: ليلى الأخيلية
rows.claim: Layla al-Akhyaliyya’s verse about al-Hajjaj calls a young adult ghulām, illustrating the word’s extended use.
rows.anchor: شفاها من الداء الذي قد أصابها ... غلام إذا هز القناة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Another poet calls himself a ghulām while describing his readiness to receive a sword’s strike.
rows.anchor: تلق ذباب السيف عني فإنني ... غلام إذا هو جيت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Ghulām may derive from ihtilām, sexual maturity, and be applied by extension to a child who will later reach that state.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصله من الاغتلام وهو شدة الشبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith gives no name for the boy or either parent.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد شيء من ذلك في الحديث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the boy corrupted things and falsely swore to his parents, who protected him from those seeking him.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر أن هذا الغلام كان يفسد ويقسم لأبويه

rows.speaker: القرطبي عن صاحب العرس والعرائس
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi transmits a story that Khidr peeled back the boy’s left shoulder and found an inscription saying he would never believe in God.
rows.anchor: وحكى القرطبي عن صاحب العرس والعرائس أن موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the ship’s damage is the result clause but killing the boy belongs to the condition; killing immediately followed their meeting, unlike the damage following boarding.
rows.anchor: جعل خرقها جزاء للشرط، وجعل قتله من جملة الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakiyyatan means free of sins because Moses had not seen wrongdoing; another view says the child had not reached the age of sin, but “without a life for a life” indicates he was grown.
rows.anchor: ومعنى زكية طاهرة من الذنوب، ووصفها بهذا الوصف لأنه لم يرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وابن محيصن حميد والزهري ونافع
rows.claim: These readers pronounce zākiyatan with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وابن محيصن

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي والحسن والجحدري وابن عامر والكوفيون
rows.claim: These readers omit the alif and double the yāʾ in zakiyyatan; Abu Hayyan says the form is more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي والحسن والجحدري وابن عامر والكوفيون زكية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read nukran with a still kāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نكرا بإسكان الكاف. وقرأ نافع

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة ويعقوب وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: These authorities read the word with ḍamma on the kāf when accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر وشيبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says nukran is less severe than imran because killing one is less than drowning the whole ship’s company.
rows.anchor: والنكر قيل: أقل من الإمر لأن قتل نفس واحدة أهون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says the killing is more terrible because the ship can be repaired but life cannot be restored.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه شيئا أنكر من الأول، لأن الخرق يمكن سده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding laka sharpens Khidr’s rebuke because Moses had already been warned, excused himself by forgetting, and again broke his promise to be patient.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله لك زجر وإغلاظ ليس في الأول لأن موقعه التساؤل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿdahā means after this story or incident; Moses says another question should end their companionship.
rows.anchor: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها أي بعد هذه القصة أو بعد هذه المسألة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read fa-lā tuṣāḥibnī with the form of mutual companionship.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فلا تصاحبني من باب المفاعلة.

rows.speaker: عيسى ويعقوب
rows.claim: Isa and Yaʿqub read fa-lā taṣḥabnī from ṣaḥiba; Isa also reads it from aṣḥaba, with possible objects “your knowledge,” “you,” or “yourself.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى ويعقوب فلا تصحبني مضارع صحب وعيسى أيضا بضم التاء

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads with fatḥa on tāʾ and bāʾ and a doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج بفتح التاء والباء وشد النون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad balaghta min ladunnī ʿudhran means Moses has excused himself and reached a valid excuse.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قد بلغت من لدني عذرا أي قد اعتذرت إلي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority assimilate the nūn of ladun into the protective nūn before first-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور من لدني بإدغام نون لدن في نون الوقاية

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Asim lighten the nūn as the final nūn of ladun; Abu Hayyan notes that this matches ordinary noun-plus-possessive morphology.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم بتخفيف النون وهي نون لدن اتصلت بياء

rows.speaker: شعبة وابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Shuʿba colors the dāl with ḍamma and a report from Asim has sukūn; Ibn Mujahid calls the latter a transmission error, but Abu Hayyan says it is a valid dialect form.
rows.anchor: وأشم شعبة الضم في الدال، وروي عن عاصم سكون الدال. قال ابن مجاهد

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith in al-Bukhari says the Prophet wished Moses had been patient so they could hear more of the story.
rows.anchor: وفي البخاري قال: «يرحم الله موسى لوددنا أنه صبر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits the Prophet’s prayer for mercy upon himself and Moses, saying patience would have shown them wonders.
rows.anchor: وأسند الطبري قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دعا لأحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The village is variously placed at Antioch, Ubulla, an Andalusian island, Barqa, Abu Huran, Nazareth, or Armenia; Abu Hayyan calls the reports confused.
rows.anchor: إنطاكية أو الأبلة أو بجزيرة الأندلس وهي الجزيرة الخضراء، أو برقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says they walked among the people’s gathering places asking for food, a lesson in the world’s low standing before God.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث أنهما كانا يمشيان على مجالس أولئك القوم يستطعمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating ahl broadens the request to the whole village, one person at a time, rather than only those first approached.
rows.anchor: وتكرر لفظ أهل على سبيل التوكيد، وقد يظهر له فائدة عن التوكيد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yuḍayyifūhumā with a doubled yāʾ from ḍayf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يضيفوهما بالتشديد من ضيف.

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير والحسن وأبو رجاء وأبو رزين وابن محيصن وعاصم وأبان
rows.claim: These readers use the light form from aḍāfa, with kasra on ḍād and sukūn on yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير والحسن وأبو رجاء وأبو رزين وابن محيصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing a wish to collapse to the wall is a striking metaphor; Arabic often assigns rational actions to animals or inanimate things, requiring no special proof.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الإرادة إلى الجدار من المجاز البليغ والاستعارة البارعة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says an ignorant distorter assigned the pronoun to Khidr because he mistook the Quran’s elevated metaphor for a lower style.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ولقد بلغني أن بعض المحرفين لكلام الله ممن لا يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan doubts the attribution to Ibn Dawud al-Isfahani of denying Quranic metaphor, since he was a consummate poet and prose stylist.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره أهل أصول الفقه عن أبي بكر محمد بن داود الأصبهاني

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yanqaḍḍ as collapse, from a bird’s swooping, on the infaʿala pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ينقض أي يسقط من انقضاض الطائر، ووزنه انفعل

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: Al-Lawāmiʿ derives the word from small gravel, so the wall crumbles into stone-sized pieces.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب اللوامح: من القضة وهي الحصى الصغار، ومنه طعام قضض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derivation makes the word afʿala from naqḍ, like aḥmar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: وزنه افعل من النقض كاحمر.

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads the verb in the passive; this reading is also transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ينقض بضم الياء وفتح القاف والضاد مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: عبد الله والأعمش
rows.claim: Their reading says the wall “wants to collapse,” with an implied subjunctive after lām.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله وقراءة الأعمش يريد لينقض كذلك

rows.speaker: علي وعكرمة وأبو شيخ خيوان بن خالد الهنائي وخليد بن سعد ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: These readers use ṣād in yinṣāṣ; Ibn Khalawayh says the form means to split lengthwise and cites Dhū al-Rumma’s munqāṣ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي وعكرمة وأبو شيخ خيوان بن خالد الهنائي وخليد بن سعد

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb’s line likening separation to a broken tooth illustrates the splitting sense.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول أبي ذؤيب: فراق كقص السن فالصبر إنه

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri is reported with yinḍāḍ, from a verb of demolition; Abu Ali says his famous reading has ṣād instead.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: ينقاض بألف وضاد معجمة وهو من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of fa-aqāmahu is that Khidr straightened the wall, rather than demolishing and rebuilding it.
rows.anchor: فأقامه الظاهر أنه لم يهدمه وبناه كما ذهب إليه بعضهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The report in Abd Allah’s codex supports demolition and rebuilding, since rebuilding would earn wages.
rows.anchor: ووقع هذا في مصحف عبد الله وأيد بقوله لاتخذت عليه أجرا

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Khidr wiped the wall with his hand and it stood.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: مسحه بيده وأقامه فقام.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Khidr propped the wall with a post.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أقامه بعمود عمده به. وقال مقاتل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid says Khidr leveled or plastered the wall.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: سواه بالشيد أي لبسه به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Khidr pushed the wall with his hand until it stood; Abu Hayyan says this best fits prophets.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: دفعه بيده فاستقام وهذا أليق بحال الأنبياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says hunger and hardship led Moses to suggest charging for the repair so they could obtain food.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: كانت الحال حال اضطرار وافتقار إلى المطعم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Moses was not directly asking, but implicitly reproached Khidr for declining wages and approved taking payment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وقوله لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا وإن لم يكن سؤالا

rows.speaker: عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وابن بحرية
rows.claim: These readers use wa-la-ttakhadhta with a form from takhadha; Basran grammarians treat tāʾ as a root, while others derive the form from akhadha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وابن بحرية ولتخذت بتاء مفتوحة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s line about placing his foot beside a camel saddle-girth witnesses the form takhadhtu.
rows.anchor: وقد تخذت رجلي إلى جنب غرزها ... نسيفا كأفحوص القطاة المطرق

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians treat tāʾ as a root in takhadha, not from akhadha; others derive it from akhadha and explain the triliteral by analogy.
rows.anchor: والتاء أصل عند البصريين وليس من الأخذ، وزعم بعضهم أن الاتخاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” points to Moses’ wage remark as the cause of separation; although not a direct question, it implies asking why Khidr did not take wages given their need.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا إشارة إلى قوله لو شئت أي هذا الإعراض سبب الفراق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes hādhā as a gesture to the impending separation at the promised time; Abu Hayyan finds his analysis questionable.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: قد تصور فراق بينهما عند حلول ميعاده

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads firāqun baynī with tanwīn, while the majority use a genitive construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة فراق بيني بالتنوين والجمهور على الإضافة.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says al-bayn means harmony between companions, a place-word used as a noun; repeating “between me and you” emphasizes it.
rows.anchor: والبين قال ابن عطية: الصلاح الذي يكون بين المصطحبين ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl explains the outcomes of the ship, boy, and wall, whose eventual reality differed from their appearance; Ibn Waththab reads sanubbiʾuka without hamza.
rows.anchor: سأنبئك أي سأخبرك بتأويل ما رأيت من خرق السفينة وقتل الغلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses objected about the ship and boy for God’s sake, but about the wall for himself, seeking worldly gain, which caused separation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: كان قول موسى في السفينة وفي الغلام لله

rows.speaker: أرباب المعاني
rows.claim: Mystical interpreters compare the incidents with Moses’ past: the ark in the Nile, killing the Egyptian, and lifting the stone for Shuʿayb’s daughters without wages.
rows.anchor: وقال أرباب المعاني: هذه الأمثلة التي وقعت لموسى مع الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses took hold of Khidr’s clothes and demanded what authorized the actions; Khidr began with the first event, the ship.
rows.anchor: روي أن موسى عليه السلام لما عزم الخضر على مفارقته أخذ بثيابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says ten brothers owned the ship, five disabled and five working at sea; another says they were hired workers, and the ship was attributed to them by association.
rows.anchor: قيل: كانت لعشرة إخوة، خمسة زمنى وخمسة يعملون في البحر.

rows.speaker: الجمهور وعلي
rows.claim: The majority read masākīn with a light sīn as the plural of miskīn; Ali doubles it, as the plural of massāk, glossed as sailors or shipmen and alternatively tanners.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: مساكين بتخفيف السين جمع مسكين. وقرأ علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading presents the ship owners as weak people deserving compassion and supports defining miskīn as someone with a basic means of living, better off than a faqīr.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الأولى تدل على أن السفينة كانت لقوم ضعفاء ينبغي أن يشفق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr’s wording “I wanted to damage it” attributes the damaging intention to himself.
rows.anchor: وقوله فأردت فيه إسناد إرادة العيب إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beneficial wall outcome is attributed to God as Lord, while the defect is not, since mentioning damage would be inappropriate in relation to God.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: فأراد ربك أن يبلغا لما في ذكر العيب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the damaging intention is foregrounded for emphasis; fear of seizure was not the sole cause, since the owners’ poverty also mattered.
rows.anchor: قلت: النية به التأخير، وإنما قدم للعناية

rows.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy and Abd Allah says “every sound ship.”
rows.anchor: وقيل في قراءة أبي وعبد الله كل سفينة صالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To damage the ship means to pierce it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أن أعيبها بخرقها.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read warāʾahum, a word meaning behind or ahead; here it means ahead, as in readings attributed to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وراءهم وهو لفظ يطلق على الخلف وعلى الأمام

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو عبيد وابن السكيت والزجاج
rows.claim: These authorities say warāʾ can mean in front, citing Quranic verses and poetry including Labid and Suwār ibn al-Muḍarrib.
rows.anchor: وكون وراءهم بمعنى أمامهم قول قتادة وأبي عبيد وابن السكيت والزجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the ordinary sense “behind,” but in time: seizure by the king would follow their present work; uses such as “before the Quran” are likewise temporal.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وقوله وراءهم عندي هو على بابه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: For those reading amāmahum, Ibn Atiyya says ahead is spatial because the travelers were heading toward the king’s country; the Prophet’s “prayer is ahead” is spatial too.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ أمامهم أراد في المكان أي أنهم كانوا يسيرون إلى بلده

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the king was in front, citing Hell as being in front of people; Ibn Atiyya calls the argument unsound and cites al-Zajjaj’s criticism.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أمامهم ألا ترى أنه يقول من ورائهم جهنم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says ahead and behind can both describe time: what approaches becomes behind once it catches up, and before reaching it can be called ahead.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لا يجوز أن يقال للرجل بين يديك هو وراءك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the travelers were returning along a route that passed the king, warāʾahum could mean literally behind them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز إن كان رجوعهم في طريقهم على الغاصب فكان وراءهم حقيقة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says warāʾ meaning ahead is an extension: with objects lacking a front, each of two opposed sides can be behind the other; most linguists treat the word as an antonym.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: إنما جاز استعمال وراء بمعنى أمام على الاتساع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports name the king Hudad ibn Budad, an unbeliever, or al-Julanda, king of Ghassan.
rows.anchor: قيل: واسم هذا الملك هدد بن بدد وكان كافرا. وقيل: الجلندى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits that the boy was an unbeliever; Ubayy’s codex and Ibn Abbas’s reading make this explicit, and the hadith says he was fixed upon unbelief.
rows.anchor: وقوله فكان أبواه مؤمنين في هذا حذف وهو أن المعنى وكان كافرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads that the boy was an unbeliever while his parents were believers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: وأما الغلام فكان كافرا وكان أبواه مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abawayhi means father and mother through a nonproductive dual formed by dominance, like the dual of sun and moon.
rows.anchor: ويراد بأبويه أبوه وأمه ثني تغليبا من باب القمرين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والجحدري
rows.claim: They read abawāhu muʾminān; grammarians explain the form through an implied subject, pronoun of the matter, or a dialect of Banū al-Harith.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو سعيد الخدري والجحدري: فكان أبواه مؤمنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashīnā means fearing that the child’s tyranny and unbelief would burden, corrupt, or lead his believing parents astray through disobedience and harm.
rows.anchor: فخشينا أي خفنا أن يغشي الوالدين المؤمنين طغيانا عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr feared this because God revealed the boy’s inner state and commanded his killing to remove a known corruption.
rows.anchor: وإنما خشي الخضر منه ذلك لأن الله عز وعلا أعلمه بحاله

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads “your Lord feared,” interpreted as God disliking the outcome and changing it.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي فخاف ربك، والمعنى فكره ربك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the plural to quote God’s speech meaning “we disliked,” as in the angel’s “that I may give you.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قوله فخشينا حكاية لقول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan links the phrase about removing the boy to prevent future corruption with the Muʿtazilite doctrine of two appointed lifespans.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله كاخترامه لمفسدة عرفها في حياته مذهب المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent plural “we feared” refers to Khidr and righteous companions who shared the concern; another view makes it refer to God through Khidr.
rows.anchor: والظاهر إسناد فعل الخشية في خشينا إلى ضمير الخضر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows the plural to refer to God, with Khidr voicing His words; al-Tabari explains it as God’s disliking the outcome.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو في جهة الله وعنه عبر الخضر وهو الذي قال فيه الزمخشري

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the best account, despite tension with the wording, is metaphor from the human perspective: people would fear harm to the parents if they knew the boy’s state.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والأظهر عندي في توجيه هذا التأويل وإن كان اللفظ

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads “your Lord feared”; Ibn Atiyya says this makes the metaphor in divine speech clear, as with Quranic laʿalla and ʿasā, which express human-relative expectation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود فخاف ربك، وهذا بين الاستعارة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yurhiqihimā means to burden or compel them severely; the child’s love would make them follow him.
rows.anchor: ويرهقهما معناه يجشمهما ويكلفهما بشدة، والمعنى أن يلقيهما

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وشيبة وحميد والأعمش وابن جرير
rows.claim: These readers double the dāl in yubdilahumā here and in al-Tahrim and al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر وشيبة وحميد والأعمش وابن جرير

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة والحسن وابن محيصن
rows.claim: The other canonical readers, Hasan, and Ibn Muhaysin read without doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة والحسن وابن محيصن بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakātan means purity from sins together with noble character and tranquility; aqraba is not comparative because the boy had neither purity nor mercy.
rows.anchor: والزكاة هنا الطهارة والنقاء من الذنوب وما ينطوي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of aqraba raḥman is a child who shows greater mercy to his parents; Ibn Jurayj says they would love him.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله وأقرب رحما أي رحمة والديه وقال ابن جريج

rows.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
rows.claim: Ruʾba’s line uses raḥm as evidence for the word’s meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال رؤبة بن العجاج: يا منزل الرحم على إدريسا

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: These authorities read raḥman with ḍamma on ḥāʾ; Ibn Abbas reads with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر في رواية ويعقوب وأبو حاتم رحما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view derives raḥm from kinship, making the replacement child closer in family ties; reports identify a Muslim boy or a girl who bore a prophet, and Ibn Abbas reports seventy prophets, which Ibn Atiyya rejects as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرحم من الرحم والقرابة أي أو صل للرحم. قيل: ولدت غلاما مسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys’ orphan status indicates they were young; a hadith says orphanhood ends at puberty, and here the word expresses compassion. A report gives their names and those of their parents.
rows.anchor: ووصف الغلامين باليتم يدل على أنهما كانا صغيرين. وفي الحديث

rows.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: Ikrima and Qatada say the treasure was a large amount of buried gold and silver.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في الكنز أنه مال مدفون جسيم ذهب وفضة قاله عكرمة وقتادة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr say the treasure was knowledge in a buried codex; another report says it was a gold tablet.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن جبير: كان علما في مصحف مدفونة: وقيل: لوح من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent father is the boys’ nearest biological father; other reports place him seven or ten generations back. The boys were preserved through his righteousness.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أباهما هو الأقرب إليهما الذي ولدهما دنية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says God preserves a righteous man through his descendants.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «إن الله يحفظ الرجل الصالح في ذريته»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmatan is an object of purpose; al-Zamakhshari allows a verbal noun meaning God had mercy on them, while Abu al-Baqaʾ calls the alternative parses strained.
rows.anchor: وانتصب رحمة على المفعول له وأجاز الزمخشري أن ينصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr says he acted by God’s command rather than his own reasoning, indicating that he was a prophet receiving revelation.
rows.anchor: وما فعلته أي وما فعلت ما رأيت من خرق السفينة

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit lists four forms of “I can”; Abu Hayyan explains the dropped element in istaṭāʿ as the inflectional tāʾ, replaced by ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: يقال ما أستطيع وما أسطيع وما أستتيع وأستيع

rows.speaker: أهل التحرير والتحبير
rows.claim: Al-Tahrir wa al-Tahbir condemns using Moses’ encounter with Khidr to claim Khidr or a saint is superior to a prophet, calling the argument self-delusion.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب التحرير والتحبير ما نصه: تعلق بعض الجهال بما جرى

rows.speaker: ابن العربي الطائي الحاتمي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi claimed saints outrank prophets because they take directly from God while prophets are mediated; Abu Hayyan denounces this and the related claims as heresy and extremist unity doctrine.
rows.anchor: وهكذا سمعنا من يحكي هذه المقالة عن بعض الضالين المضلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sadd means a barrier or partition and is read with either ḍamma or fatḥa.
rows.anchor: السد الحاجز والحائل بين الشيئين، ويقال بالضم وبالفتح.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Radm means a barrier, perhaps a stronger one made by piling material; another gloss makes it the filling of gaps, illustrated by Antara’s line about poetry leaving no gap.
rows.anchor: الردم: السد. وقيل: الردم أكبر من السد لأن الردم ما جعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubrah means a mass or piece from gathering together; the lion’s mane gathers on its shoulder, and zabara a book is to collect its letters.
rows.anchor: الزبرة: القطعة وأصله الاجتماع، ومنه زبرة الأسد لما اجتمع

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari defines the ṣadafān as mountain sides facing or meeting because of their closeness; readings vary, with fatḥa attributed to Tamim and ḍamma to Himyar.
rows.anchor: الصدفان جانبا الجبل إذا تحاذيا لتقاربهما أو لتلاقيهما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says ṣadaf is any great, high structure.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الصدف كل بناء عظيم مرتفع.

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most authorities identify al-qiṭr as molten copper; others say it is molten iron or lead.
rows.anchor: القطر النحاس المذاب في قول الأكثرين. وقيل: الحديد المذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqb is the verbal noun for digging and cutting through; ghiṭāʾ means a cover, plural aghṭiya, from the verb for concealing.
rows.anchor: النقب مصدر نقب أي حفر وقطع. الغطاء معروف وجمعه أغطية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says firdaws is a garden containing grapevines.
rows.anchor: الفردوس قال الفراء: البستان الذي فيه الكرم.

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab says any enclosed garden is a firdaws.
rows.anchor: وقال ثعلب: كل بستان يحوط عليه فهو فردوس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The residents’ contentment is the highest description: worldly people always seek greater pleasure, while the phrase may also simply deny transition and reinforce eternal stay.
rows.anchor: وهذه غاية الوصف لأن الإنسان في الدنيا في أي نعيم كان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya glosses ḥawlan as transition.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والحول بمعنى التحول.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses it as moving away.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد متحولا. وقال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem says every dynasty has an end and then receives a turn or change; Abu Hayyan questions whether ḥawl is a collective with singular ḥawāla.
rows.anchor: لكل دولة أجل ... ثم يتاح لها حول

rows.speaker: الزجاج عن قوم
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports an interpretation of ḥawl as a trick for changing place, but calls it weak and forced.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج عن قوم: هي بمعنى الحيلة في التنقل وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One occasion report says Jews challenged Muhammad’s universal prophethood and cited his inability to answer their question about the Spirit; the verse teaches the unbounded scope of God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: قيل سبب نزولها أن اليهود قالوا للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Huyayy ibn Akhtab cited the verses about wisdom and limited knowledge; this verse explains that such good is only a drop compared with God’s words.
rows.anchor: وقيل قال حيي بن أخطب في كتابكم ومن يؤت الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea is water used as ink; the Lord’s words mean His knowledge and wisdom, infinite unlike the finite sea, so the Prophet knows only what is revealed.
rows.anchor: قل لو كان البحر أي ماء البحر مدادا وهو ما يمد به الدواة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read midādan; Abd Allah, Ibn Abbas, al-Aʿmash, Mujahid, al-Aʿraj, Hasan, and al-Munqari from Abu Amr read mudadan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور مدادا لكلمات ربي. وقرأ عبد الله وابن عباس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read tanfadu with tāʾ; Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, Amr ibn Ubayd, al-Aʿmash, Talha, and Ibn Abi Layla read with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تنفد بالتاء من فوق. وقرأ حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads an tanfada with a doubled form, also reported from Asim and Abu Amr; Abu Hayyan distinguishes it from the canonical passive of anfada.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي أن تنفد بالتشديد على تفعل على المضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishtiʿāl describes fire spreading and branching in an intense blaze; shayb is gray hair after another hair color.
rows.anchor: اشتغال النار تفرقها في التهابها فصارت شعلا. وقيل: شعاع النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makhāḍ is the intensifying pain and contractions of childbirth; jidhʿ is the trunk between the ground and branches, also sometimes a branch itself.
rows.anchor: المخاض اشتداد وجع الولادة والطلق. الجذع ما بين الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarī can mean high in rank, or a small stream whose water flows through it; the two senses have different root endings.
rows.anchor: السري المرتفع القدر، يقال سرو يسرو، ويجمع على سراة

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s verse uses sarā for a small watercourse or channel.
rows.anchor: وقال لبيد: فتوسطا عرض السرى فصدعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hazz means movement; ruṭab are dates picked before hardening and drying, with the irregular plural arṭāb.
rows.anchor: الهز التحريك. الرطب معروف واحده رطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janī means ripe and fit for picking; Abu Amr says it is not dried, another view says softened from unripe dates, and al-Farra equates it with harvested fruit.
rows.anchor: الجني ما طاب وصلح للاجتناء. وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurrat al-ʿayn derives from coolness: joy has cool tears and grief warm tears; Quraysh and Najd differ in the verb’s vowel.
rows.anchor: قرة العين: مأخوذ من القر، يقال: دمع الفرح اللمس

rows.speaker: أبو تمام
rows.claim: Abu Tammam’s verse contrasts lovers’ heated eyes with cool eyes of those who rejoice in another’s misfortune.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو تمام: فأما عيون العاشقين فأسخنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fariyy can mean something immense in good or evil; it derives from cutting, and the proverb describes a major deed or statement. Al-Zamakhshari calls it novel or wondrous.
rows.anchor: الفري العظيم من الأمر يستعمل في الخير وفي الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gesture may use the hand, eye, garment, head, or mouth; ishāra’s alif derives from yāʾ, and a poem by Kathir witnesses the related form.
rows.anchor: الإشارة معروفة تكون باليد والعين والثوب والرأس والفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
rows.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes dhikru the predicate of an omitted subject, “this recited text is a mention”; another makes it the predicate of kāf-hā-yā-ʿayn-ṣād, a view attributed to al-Farra and judged strained because the meanings do not match.
rows.anchor: وذكر خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هذا المتلو من هذا القرآن ذكر. وقيل ذكر خبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parse makes dhikru the subject and omits its predicate, understood as “in what is recited.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: ذكر مبتدأ والخبر محذوف تقديره فيما يتلى ذكر.

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن ونافع
rows.claim: The majority read kāf with a still fāʾ; Hasan has a reported ḍamma, and Nafiʿ inclines hāʾ and yāʾ between full sound and imāla.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور كاف بإسكان الفاء. وروي عن الحسن ضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dāl of dhālika is articulated clearly before ṣād.
rows.anchor: وأظهر دال صاد عند ذاك. ذكر وقرأ الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Reports give Hasan several vowelings of hāʾ and yāʾ, Asim ḍamma on yāʾ or kasra on both, and Hamza fatḥa on hāʾ with kasra on yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ذكر وقرأ الحسن بضم الهاء وعنه أيضا ضم الياء وكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani says the apparent ḍamma on hāʾ and yāʾ is emphatic coloring, not a true ḍamma that would change the next letter.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو الداني: معنى الضم في الهاء والياء إشباع التفخيم

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل عبد الرحمن بن أحمد بن الحسن المقري الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi records additional anomalous vowelings and explains they are not true ḍammas, but Hijazi-style alif tafkhim approaching wāw; a true ḍamma would turn the following alif into wāw.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفضل عبد الرحمن بن أحمد بن الحسن المقري الرازي في كتاب اللوامح
